newsitem.title: ITALY: Thirty alleged mobsters set free in Naples.
newsitem.headline: Thirty alleged mobsters set free in Naples.

text.p: Thirty alleged mobsters on trial for the murder of an 11-year-old boy during a clan gunfight have been released from jail because court procedures were taking too long, a prosecutor said on Thursday.

A judge ordered the release of the suspected members of the Camorra, the Naples Mafia, on Wednesday night because their trial is lasting longer than the legal limit on preventive custody, Naples anti-mob prosecutor Luigi Bobbio told Reuters.
The trial has lasted more than five years and is still only in its initial stages. Although the suspects have been freed, the charges have not been dropped and the case will continue.
In a separate incident on Thursday, Naples prefect Achille Catalani suspended the local council in Ottaviano, a town near Naples, for being under the influence of organised crime.

The Camorra problem came to a head earlier this week when the Italian government said it would send some 500 troops into Naples to help counter a recent wave of clan fighting that has claimed some 80 lives since the start of the year.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left cabinet is expected to approve the emergency measures on Friday.

"This shows the schizophrenia of Naples' justice system. On the one hand we send in the army to battle the Camorra and on the other we let 30 bosses go," one senior police source told Reuters on Thursday, declining to be named.
Prosecutors have often criticised the slowness of the judicial system, which they say is bogged down by complicated court procedures and frequent strikes by lawyers.
"If we don't change the rules urgently, the risks will become even greater," Bobbio said.
Naples Mayor Antonio Bassolino called this week for a reform of the system, saying that many people arrested for events tied to organised crime return too soon to freedom.
Among the 30 released on Thursday were Ciro and Salvatore Puccinelli, the suspected bosses of a clan that operates in the Fuorigrotta district in northwest Naples.
Bobbio said he had asked that the released suspects not be allowed to leave the country and be required to sign a court register three times a week. He said he was awaiting a response from the court.
Some 82 people are on trial for the gunfight that broke out between two rival clans in July 1991, killing 11-year-old Fabio de Pandi and two other innocent bystanders.
Authorities have already had to set free another 12 suspects from the case because of expired custody limits, according to Bobbio.
